claims.claim: The containment helper rejects an otherwise contained path whenever its root-relative name begins with two dots, including a literal '..cache' first component, so callers treating null as out-of-root can omit that path.
claims.actor: K1 path-containment helper and dependent hook checks
claims.trigger: A caller resolves a contained path whose first root-relative component starts with '..'.
claims.exceptions: Actual parent traversal, the root itself and absolute relative results are also rejected; downstream relevance filters may independently exclude some paths.
claims.enforcement_effect: Potential checking omission; helper branch is explicit, end-to-end relevant-file effect remains to be traced.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Implementation attribution and active-root policy do not express rejection of contained dot-prefixed names.
Containment helpers are implementation; event configuration does not register this broader exclusion.
Prior claim says in-root path resolution and quotes dispatcher calls, but does not identify a contained '..cache' path as rejected. Root selection is a separate action.

claims.comparison_reason: A containment exclusion and an exclusion by the first two characters are behaviorally different. Normative relevance of the latter remains open, so this is not counted as proven novel.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: For root C:/repo and an ordinary contained C:/repo/..cache/package.json, path.relative yields '..cache/package.json'; startsWith('..') rejects it despite no traversal. Trace whether any applicable manifest/change check would otherwise inspect it.
claims.confidence: HIGH for source branch; MEDIUM for effective normative relevance
claims.open_question: Does a valid relevant file under a contained dot-prefixed root child reach this helper and lose checks, and should that omission be registered as an effective constraint rather than an incidental parser defect?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Executable-enforcement pass: inspect all relInside callers and copy only pure path predicates into a side-effect-free probe.
